title: feat(core, plugin-security)!: permission sets resolve by (package, name), and a package position's sets resolve from its package (ADR-0150 E3)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi99Aqw5TrjgthJiwHzU17N9R)_

Fixes #31674

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: follow-up #31819
Narrowing: (1) a package position's bare reference to a permission set whose only holder is an environment-authored item, or whose only body is the metadata service's, D3 (a) (not measurable first-party: no first-party package tree holds an environment item; the dogfood boot refused 0); (2) a package position's bare reference to a permission set whose only holder is a package outside the position package's declared closure, per the epic seat's reading 6728487836 (first-party: 0). Sibling in the same release artifact: 0. Measured statically over every first-party position declaration: the showcase's positions name only showcase sets, app-crm's positions name only its own set, and the built-in positions name only the security plugin's own sets (the audience anchors are the environment's reference, below). HotCRM is outside this session's repository access: NOT MEASURED.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：安全目录里的权限集改按（软件包, 名称）解析，走 core 里同一条包寻址规则和 metadata-core 里同一个依赖闭包。职位引用权限集时，从声明这个职位的软件包去解析：本包的、它声明依赖的包的、或 `sys` 的；够不着就拒绝并列出每个候选。职位本身不变（仍是环境级一个名字一个持有者）。
- 为什么改：专题 #31527 的子卡 E3（ADR-0150 D3/D4/D7）。以前按名字取第一个注册的权限集，一个包的职位可能拿到别的包或环境里同名的权限集，取哪个看注册顺序，也没有任何提示。
- 风险与回滚：只有「包里的职位引用了本包够不着的权限集」的部署会看到变化：那个职位不再通过这个名字授权，启动时的目录引用报告逐个列出职位和每个候选。存储的授权、环境自建的职位、管理员对包职位的覆盖、everyone/guest 锚点仍按整个环境解析，行为不变。第一方实测 0 个。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts` 的 `referenceCaller` 与 `resolvePermissionScoped`（谁算调用方、拒绝时不回退）；`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` 的 `catalogSetBody`（授权路径把职位传进去）；`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/catalog-reference-report.ts`（拒绝写进报告）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run src/security-catalog-permission-sets-by-package.test.ts`，预期 14 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

Permission sets are behavioural metadata (ADR-0150 D1 bucket 2), so the security catalog now reads them by `(package, name)`. Positions and capabilities are unchanged.

- **`@objectstack/core` `security/security-catalog.ts`.** A registry that carries the package-scoped reads (`packageScopedHoldersOf`, `getPackageScopedItem`, `getEnvironmentScopedItem`, `getArtifactItem`) is read by `(package, name)` for permission sets. ObjectQL's `SchemaRegistry` carries all of them. The catalog calls the one rule, `resolvePackageScopedHolders` (R/R2), over the registry's holders, with the one closure walk, `packageResolutionClosure` (`@objectstack/metadata-core`). That is the same holder set objectql's `resolvePackageScopedName` hands the rule. ⛔ No second rule, no second closure, no first-registered fallback, no injected resolver.
  - **Who asks.** A position's `permissionSets` resolve as a caller in the package that shipped the position (`resolve(type, name, { position })`). Four kinds of reference are the environment's, resolved as a caller with no package: a stored grant (it carries only the name until ADR-0150 D8), an environment-authored position, an administrator's overlay or `.custom` override of a package's position (told apart from the shipped item by `getArtifactItem`), and the audience anchors `everyone` and `guest`.
  - **A refusal confers nothing.** `resolve` answers `undefined`. The new `resolveReference` returns the refusal with every candidate, in the rule's words.
  - **The registry's answer is final.** A holder the rule resolved that may not be served (a disabled package's set) is not-found, never a second by-name read. The metadata service is read only for a name the registry holds nowhere. It reads by name only, so its body is the environment's: a caller with no package is served it, and for a package's reference it is the D3 (a) refusal (`outside-closure`, naming the environment, in the rule's message), so the boot report and the delegated-admin boundary still name it.
  - **The list** has one entry per `(package, name)` holder plus the environment's own item.
  - A registry carrying only some of the package-scoped reads is refused at construction. A by-name stand-in (a test double without the holder reads) is read by name, as before.
- **`@objectstack/core` `security/resolve-authz-context.ts`.** Every position-bound set read passes its position: the position grants in force, the guest anchor, and §6a/6b. A set one position cannot resolve is still granted through another position that can.
- **`@objectstack/plugin-security`.**
  - `delegated-admin-gate.ts`: the organization boundary and the delegate's scope resolve a position's sets from that position. A refusal is the boundary failure, and its reason carries the refusal.
  - `catalog-reference-report.ts`: a position's unresolved sets now carry `refusals` (each set with its reason and every candidate), in the log line and its meta.
  - `access-upgrade-check.ts`: the projected catalog passes the reference scope through.
- **Package edge.** `@objectstack/core` moves `@objectstack/metadata-core` from devDependencies to dependencies (seat amendment). No cycle: metadata-core depends on spec and zod, and spec depends on no workspace package. `check:lean-entry-closure` holds its admitted set (15 packages), and `core-boundary.ratchet` is green.
- **`scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.mjs`** (outside the card's file surface, forced by the edge above). The census evaluates each source as CommonJS. Through core's barrel, it now reaches metadata-core's `createRequire(import.meta.url)`, which has no CommonJS spelling. The loader hands such a module its own file URL. It is the only loader of its kind in `scripts/`.

## Tests

- `packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.test.ts` (+12, two of them extended in review round 1). These pin the catalog's plumbing around the rule, over a stand-in registry with the package-scoped reads:
  - a refusal confers nothing and names every candidate, with no fallback;
  - two holders in the closure, and two environment-wide, are refused, naming both;
  - who asks: package positions, the environment's positions, anchors, stack positions;
  - a name the registry holds nowhere: the metadata service's body serves a caller with no package, and is the D3 (a) refusal naming the environment for a package's reference;
  - a resolved holder that may not be served (a disabled package's set, with a metadata-service body of that name) is final: not-found for every caller;
  - the list is keyed per holder;
  - positions and capabilities are read by name;
  - partial registries are refused, and by-name stand-ins stay by-name;
  - a throwing read is `AuthzStoreUnavailable`.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-catalog-permission-sets-by-package.test.ts` (new, 14), over the real `SchemaRegistry` and core's grant path:
  - the own set, a `sys` set and a dependency's set resolve;
  - an environment-only set is refused (D3 (a)), and so is an outside-closure package set, each naming its holder and each granting nothing; the by-name read is asserted to have served both on base;
  - a set refused for one position is still granted through another position;
  - stored grants, environment positions and administrator overlays resolve environment-wide;
  - the `everyone` anchor binds an accepted package `isDefault` set, and a second package holding that name is refused at registration, naming both, while the anchor keeps the first;
  - the list is keyed per holder;
  - every package-less read and the list equal the by-name read under phase 1;
  - a same-name position from a second package is still refused (D7).
- `delegated-admin-gate-catalog.test.ts` (+1): the scoped organization boundary refuses an out-of-closure set, naming its holder.
- `catalog-reference-report.test.ts` (+1): the report lists an out-of-closure set with the refusal naming every candidate.

**Forced test changes** (rigs that served sets a booted kernel's registry holds, and so read as the narrowing):

- `catalog-reference-report.test.ts` and `delegable-scope-no-identity-positions.posture.test.ts`: the stubbed manifest service now registers the plugin's own permission sets into the engine registry under the plugin, as a booted kernel does. Before, they were served only from a stand-in metadata service, which in a booted kernel does not carry them (the catalog doc's measurement table). Without this, the built-in `org_external` position could not reach `external_default`.
- `catalog-reference-report.test.ts`, the "listed per position" block: the binding position's package now declares the set package, and the set package also ships the auditor set. The outside-closure case uses a second package that declares nothing.

## Acceptance notes

- **The epic's red lines.** (1) Never loosens: no first-registered fallback, no second lookup once the registry has answered, no environment-wide guess. Each pin was ablated (below). (2) Every refusal names every candidate, in the rule's words, in `resolveReference`, the boundary failure and the boot report. (3) Independently releasable: ADR-0150's readings, below.
- **ADR-0150 readings.**
  - (a) The phase-1 one-holder tests stay green. `registry-security-catalog-namespace` is untouched, and the D7 pin here shows a second same-name position is still refused.
  - (b) Bare-name behaviour is unchanged for every name with one holder and a package-less or in-closure caller. The parity pin over the real registry checks every package-less read and the list against the by-name read. The only change is the declared narrowing.
  - (c) No migration.
  - (d) `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The protocol is unchanged, and the changeset carries `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
- **The audience anchors (the epic seat's reading).** `everyone` and `guest` are registered by the security plugin, but `declareEveryone` composes their sets from the deployment's baseline plus every package `isDefault` set an administrator accepted (`readAcceptedEveryoneSets`, ADR-0090 D5/D9). That is the environment's binding (ADR-0150 D7), so the anchors resolve as a caller with no package. Read from the security plugin's package, the rule would refuse an accepted app default, such as the showcase's `showcase_member_default`, as outside the closure. Child A records this reading in ADR-0150.
- **A set only the metadata service holds**, read by a package's position, is the D3 (a) refusal naming the environment (ruled in review round 1). In a booted kernel the engine registry holds every permission set, so this refuses nothing there (the catalog's measurement table, and the dogfood below); it is counted in the D3 (a) arm of the Narrowing line.
- **Out of scope.** `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts` builds a catalog over a stand-in registry and stays by name: #31817.
- **New public names** (the seat's call): `SecurityCatalogReader.resolveReference`, `resolveCatalogReference`, `SecurityCatalogReferenceScope`, `SecurityCatalogResolution`, `SecurityCatalogPackageScopedRegistry`, and `PositionNamingUnresolvedSets.refusals`.

<details><summary>Ablation readings (each through scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, core rebuilt and checked by ablation-dist-preflight; restored, blob == HEAD, git diff HEAD empty)</summary>

1. A refusal falls back to the registry's first-registered read: core 1 failed / 25; plugin-security 5 failed / 39 (D3 (a), outside-closure, a second position still grants, the boundary refusal, the report's refusal).
2. A position's reference asks as no package: core 5 failed / 26; plugin-security 5 failed / 39.
3. The audience anchors ask as the security plugin's package: core 1 failed / 26; plugin-security 2 failed / 39 (both anchor pins).
4. The list picks one entry per name: core 1 failed / 26. Plugin-security stays green, as designed: under phase 1 every name has one holder, so the real registry cannot tell the two lists apart.
5. The grant path drops the position: plugin-security 3 failed / 39 (D3 (a), outside-closure, a second position still grants). Core's catalog suite stays green (the mutation is outside the catalog).
6. The census loader without the `import.meta.url` hand-off: `check:platform-object-tenancy-census` exits 1 (SyntaxError: Cannot use 'import.meta' outside a module).
7. (Round 1, item 1) A resolved holder that may not be served falls through to the metadata service: core 1 failed / 26 (the disabled-package pin).
8. (Round 1, item 2) A package's reference to a metadata-only set answers not-found: core 1 failed / 26 (the D3 (a) refusal pin).

After restoring, `ablation-dist-preflight @objectstack/core E3_ABLATION --absent`: the marker is absent from all 14 built files, and the tree is clean against HEAD.

</details>

## Review round 1 (epic seat 6732998040), answered

- Item 1: once the registry has answered, its answer is final. A resolved holder that may not be served is not-found, and the metadata service is read only for a name the registry holds nowhere. Pinned, red without the fix (ablation 7).
- Item 2: a set only the metadata service holds, read by a package's position, is the D3 (a) refusal naming the environment, never not-found and never served. Pinned, red without the fix (ablation 8).
- Q2: the CLI catalog is #31817. Skills-docs: #31819.

## Verification

All readings are on head `f2f8b4ff`, which carries both round-1 fixes.

Results: 440 files passed and 3 skipped (443); 3654 tests passed and 41 skipped. The boot's catalog reference report logged no refusal in the whole run: 0 lines for `outside-closure`, `ambiguous-in-closure` or `ambiguous-in-environment`. That is the first-party count, measured on a boot.
